'''''Astragalus boeticus''''', the '''yellow milk vetch''', or '''Swedish coffee''' is a species of annual herb in the family [[Fabaceae]]. It is native to the Mediterranean and the Middle East.<ref name=":1" /> 

== Description ==
''Astragalus boeticus'' has a self-supporting growth form and compound, broad leaves.<ref>{{Cite web|title=''Astragalus boeticus'' L. - Encyclopedia of Life|url=https://eol.org/pages/703040|access-date=2022-02-04|website=eol.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Mifsud|first=Stephen|date=2002-08-23|title=''Asplenium sagittatum'' (Mule's Fern) : MaltaWildPlants.com - the online Flora of the Maltese Islands.|url=https://www.maltawildplants.com/ASPL/Asplenium_sagittatum.php|access-date=2022-02-07|website=www.maltawildplants.com|language=en-us}}</ref>

It can grow to 0.6 meters (2 feet). The bloom period is between the months of July to August. The plant has both male and female organs. It can fix nitrogen. It is pollinated by bees, moths, and butterflies.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=''Astragalus boeticus'' Swedish Coffee PFAF Plant Database |url=https://pfaf.org/User/Plant.aspx?LatinName=Astragalus+boeticus |access-date=2023-08-01 |website=pfaf.org}}</ref> 

It is most commonly found in March and April. It is most commonly found in Spain, being found more than 500 times there.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=''Astragalus boeticus'' L. |url=https://www.gbif.org/species/5344663/metrics |access-date=2023-08-01 |website=www.gbif.org |language=en}}</ref> 

== Distribution ==
''Astragalus boeticus'' is native to North Africa, southern Europe (including France) and Western Asia to Iran. It is an introduced species in northern Europe.<ref name=POWO/>

== Uses ==
The seed pods are edible. Roasted seeds are used as a substitute of coffee.<ref name=":0" />

It has been used as a coffee substitute, especially during the 1800s, when coffee was scarce. It was even used by the Swedish monarchy. There is evidence that ''Astragalus boeticus'' has a lot of genetic diversity, as it is found in most of the Mediterranean and parts of the Middle East. Evidence suggests with limited breeding that it could be a better coffee substitute.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Prohens |first=Jaime |last2=Andújar |first2=Isabel |last3=Vilanova |first3=Santiago |last4=Plazas |first4=Mariola |last5=Gramazio |first5=Pietro |last6=Prohens |first6=Rafael |last7=Herraiz |first7=Francisco J. |last8=De Ron |first8=Antonio M. |date=2014-01-01 |title=Swedish coffee (''Astragalus boeticus'' L.), a neglected coffee substitute with a past and a potential future |url=https://doi.org/10.1007/s10722-013-0059-0 |journal=Genetic Resources and Crop Evolution |language=en |volume=61 |issue=1 |pages=287–297 |doi=10.1007/s10722-013-0059-0 |issn=1573-5109|hdl=10251/64447 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>
